thread.title: Rogersville fires fire chief, passes 26-27 budget - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Rogersville fires fire chief, passes 26-27 budget - NewsBreak

author: JOHN CATE
title: Rogersville fires fire chief, passes 26-27 budget - NewsBreak
text:
By JOHN CATE ,
16 hours ago The Rogersville Board of Mayor and Aldermen held a special called meeting Tuesday evening, June 30 to pass its FY 2026-27 budget, but also dismissed a longtime employee of the town following a closed session.
The board voted in open session without dissent to terminate the employment of Kelsie Price, the town's Fire Chief since 2021 and also its Water Superintendent. Price has been part of the Rogersville Water Department since 1990, and its Fire Department since 2007.
Price's situation was a major point of debate in both the BMA meeting and the water board meeting held immediately prior to the BMA. A lengthy closed session on the matter caused the BMA meeting to start about 15 minutes late, and a similarly lengthy closed session took place toward the end of the BMA meeting to discuss the water board's recommendations.
When the meeting went back into open session, a motion was called on termination, which saw five aldermen vote for the motion; Vice-Mayor Brady Forgety abstained. All six were present for the meeting.
Price was on administrative leave and will remain on it until his termination is official on Aug. 14.
No details on why Price was terminated were given at the meeting, but Mayor John Metz issued a public statement on Wednesday night, which is printed in this issue of the Review.
Budget vote
The budget had already passed on its first reading at the town's regular BMA meeting earlier this month. Some slight adjustments to the numbers from the first draft had since been made, which Forgety went over before the board voted.
Forgety, who heads up the budget committee, stated that he had a lot to learn about the process after joining the BMA following his election last June. He credited Linda Winegar and Deputy City Recorder Cindy Andies with getting him up to speed and helping get the budget drawn up.
Since the first reading, the town had received certified figures from the state on its new tax rate following thius year's reappraisal process. The rate, which had been $1.83650 per $100 valuation, dropped to $1.2813, a number very slightly different from what had been previously estimated ($1.2775). One cent on the tax rate equals $17,500 in revenue for the town.
Total expenditures for 2026-27 will be $8,594,963 against revenue of $8,053,380. The town will balance the budget by using $541,583 from its existing fund balance.
Metz stated that the drawdown will assist the town in getting some "much-needed maintenance" done, and that the town will still have reserves of 45 percent of one year's budget, well above the 35 percent benchmark that a town wants to have.
Forgety stated that the budget contains a cost of living adjustment (COLA) for town employees.
Vice-Mayor Forgety and the other five aldermen all voted for the budget.
Other business
Prior to the discussion about the budget and Price's sitiuation, the board unanimously passed the 2026-27 pay scale for the water department and the final amendments to the 2025-26 budget. These amendments did not cause any drawdowns on the fund balance. The town was $50,156 in the black at the end of the fiscal year, returning that money to the fund balance.

The board voted in open session without dissent to terminate the employment of Kelsie Price, the town's Fire Chief since 2021 and also its Water Superintendent. Forgety, who heads up the budget committee, stated that he had a lot to learn about the process after joining the BMA following his election last June.
